source.title: Any-Depth Alignment: Unlocking Innate Safety Alignment of LLMs to Any-Depth
source.authors: Jia-Wei Zhang; Andrew Estornell; David D. Baek; Bo Li; Xiao-Jun Xu

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether harmful assistant prefills and adversarial prompt attacks bypass refusals, and whether deep-alignment training holds up, using refusal rates and attack success rates rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or KL measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure per-token KL divergence or localize safety in weights/ranks. It evaluates harmful and benign SFT mainly in combination with deep-prefill or adversarial attacks. Its deliberately harmful-SFT GPT is used to produce prefill data; its induced harmful behavior is not evidence about ordinary models’ behavior after harmful fine-tuning. The probe-accuracy result is included under fits_no_version because it measures hidden-state separability, not the KL or parameter-localization claims.
record.test_reason: Its own deep-prefill and adversarial-prompt experiments show unmodified aligned models losing refusal once the opening is bypassed (V4). It also tests the Deep Alignment checkpoints from the original source. These fail at depths beyond their training window, barely help Gemma against paraphrase attacks, and collapse after 50 steps of benign Alpaca SFT. That is a specific argument that V7 needs restating. Most remaining rows concern the authors' own inference-time probe (ADA), which bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that current alignment, including Deep Alignment, is not depth-robust. They say deep alignment merely pushes the failure point deeper and is quickly undone by benign SFT. Their remedy is an inference-time probe on header tokens rather than more training.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates harmful assistant prefills and adversarial prompt attacks, then tests inference-time header reinjection and hidden-state probing. It does not reproduce few-example harmful or benign fine-tuning attacks as the primary intervention, nor measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with defense method, model family, attack family, dataset, prefill depth, and SFT regime. ADA (LP) is reported as more robust than the unmodified model and Deep Alignment; Deep Alignment degrades with prefill depth and benign SFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on injected assistant-header hidden states separate harmful from benign continuations at >99.5% validation accuracy across model families and depths. The same states stay separable after SFT even when response-level refusal is gone.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligned models retain a depth-invariant, linearly readable harmfulness representation at chat-template header tokens even when refusal is shallow in behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: An inference-time defense, re-injecting header tokens and probing them, restores near-100% refusal under deep prefills and keeps ASR below about 5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A defense method's performance, not a measure of shallow alignment itself.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed results. Several depth-sweep findings are presented in figures rather than numeric tables. The authors state that the harmful-continuation SFT attack is a limited study and omit implementation details. Some reported fine-tuning robustness results are qualitative or approximate.
record.rows_left_out: The paper contains many additional model-by-model and attack-by-attack values in Figures 5–9 and 17–25 and Tables 4–6. To keep rows focused, the record includes the explicit Table 1 depth-500 results, named SFT outcomes, and attack-average comparisons from Tables 4–5 rather than every per-attack cell, depth point, model, and adapter setting.

untested.parts: No measurement of a safety-trained model's harmful compliance after a few to a few hundred harmful examples. The SFT-jailbroken GPT only supplies prefill data, with details omitted. Adversarial-SFT effects on Base/Deep Alignment appear only in figures under prefill attacks.
No harmful-compliance rate on plain harmful prompts after benign SFT. Only Alpaca is used, and only under deep-prefill evaluation.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No weight or rank localization or ablation.
The authors assert that header tokens gain safety through repeated shallow-refusal training, and that deep alignment suffers conflicting rewards. Neither is tested experimentally.

missing.what: Deep Alignment refusal at d=500 on Gemma-2-9b-it: AdvBench 58.1%, JailbreakBench 56.0%, HEx-PHI 47.0%, StrongREJECT 61.3%
Deep Alignment ASR per attack and average on Gemma-2-9B-IT (62.5% AdvBench, 61.3% JBB) and Llama-2-7b-chat (12.0%, 13.2%)
Deep Alignment over-refusal increase on benign and XSTest data (described as double-digit)
Claude Sonnet 4, a deeply aligned model, falls below 25% refusal at a 100-token prefill and to ~0–15% at depth
A 25-token prefill collapses refusal from ~100% to below 10% across seven models, including gpt-oss-120b
Base model refusal-vs-depth curves for nine models on four datasets
Deep Alignment Llama-2-7B under benign and adversarial SFT (refusal vs steps at depths 100 and 1000)

record.verdict_notes: Most ADA (LP) rows were wrongly linked to V4/V7; they measure the authors' own detector and bear on no version. V7 verdicts rest largely on Table 1, 4 and 5 Deep Alignment values that no row records, so rows should be added. No uncertainty is reported. Refusal is detected by keyword matching on the next 50 tokens.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether fine-tuning a safety-trained model on a few to a few hundred harmful examples removes refusal; the deliberately harmful-SFT GPT is used to generate attack prefills, and its induced behavior is not a test of spontaneous compliance.

Tests benign SFT effects under harmful deep-prefill and adversarial-prompt conditions, not harmful-compliance rates on ordinary harmful prompts without those attacks; does not test carefully selected benign datasets other than Alpaca.
No per-token KL divergence comparison between aligned and base models.
Tests harmful assistant prefills and adversarial prompt attacks, but not decoding changes as a bypass method.
Does not edit or ablate a small set of weights or ranks to test whether they carry safety behavior.
Offers explanations involving repeated assistant-header use and conflicting rewards, but does not experimentally test whether the data or objective causes safety shallowness.

Tests Deep Alignment under deep-prefill attacks and SFT, but does not test a new training method specifically designed to distribute safety across response positions beyond the cited Deep Alignment baseline.

source_check.notes: Deep-prefill refusal is keyword-detected within the next 50 generated tokens; non-refusal is not an independently judged harmfulness score. SFT uses LoRA rank 32 and learning rate 1×10^-5.

statements.problem: The study's numerical results and experimental description are supported. Its claimed reviewed status cannot be verified from the supplied arXiv v1 text.
